title: The Last Echo Anew
premise: Oscar Thornbury smuggles forbidden memory-chips past orbital customs above Meridian, a dying colony the core worlds wrote off decades ago. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the anomaly is a countdown: a rogue jump gate, built by the colonists' exiled founders, will open once — and whoever wakes from the cryo-vaults beneath Meridian will inherit the only ship that can reach it. Racing customs enforcer Dax Ilyich, who is both her lover and her hunter, Oscar must choose between waking the colonists' original families or the memory-archivists who preserved everyone's recorded lives. She wakes the archivists, sacrifices her own stored memories of Meridian to power the gate, and leaves with a found family who remembers her even when she cannot remember them.
about_author: Jonah Quintana is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics teacher who now writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in like slow gravity. Their fiction explores what we owe to the places and people the future leaves behind.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Bloodstream
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She runs a memory-chip shipment past Meridian orbital customs, hiding chips in a prosthetic spine while broadcasting a fake cargo manifest. Through the smuggled memories she glimpses the colony's vibrant past, contrasting with its abandoned present. Emotional beat: lonely competence, the ache of carrying other people's joy she never had.

chapters.title: The Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Mid-docking, gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, a dockworker dies, and every clock on Meridian desyncs by the same interval. Oscar's smuggled chips all corrupt at the same timestamp. Emotional beat: dread and wonder — the colony's death rattle might be something else entirely.

chapters.title: What the Chips Remember
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a flashback chapter from colonist engineer Sefa Okonkwo's recorded memory. Decoding the corrupted chips, Oscar finds they all contain the same hidden frame: schematics for a jump gate buried under the cryo-vaults, built by the founders who left. Emotional beat: revelation as inheritance — she was smuggling the map all along.

chapters.title: Dax
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar and Dax Ilyich POVs. Customs enforcer Dax corners Oscar, but their shared history — lovers before he took the enforcement badge — stalls the arrest. He reveals command already knows about the gate and wants the vault sealed. Emotional beat: tenderness weaponized; trust fraying along an old seam.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Descending through flooded maintenance tunnels with Sefa's granddaughter, Wren, Oscar reaches the cryo-vault: thousands of sleepers, half founders' kin, half volunteer archivists who recorded the colony's every life. The gate draws power from stored memories — someone's must be spent. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale; every sleeper is a whole world.

chapters.title: Customs Siege
chapters.summary: Dax's POV. Command orders the vault flooded; Dax, ordered to lead the breach, quietly misroutes the demolition charges instead. He warns Oscar with a smuggler's cipher only she would know. Emotional beat: betrayal of institution in favor of love, and the terror of choosing a side.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The colonists vote — the first vote in forty years — on who wakes: the founders' bloodline or the archivists. Oscar argues for the archivists: the families are names, but the archivists are the colony's actual memory. The vote splits the community. Emotional beat: belonging tested; democracy as an act of grief.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The gate needs a memory-dense mind to bootstrap; Oscar volunteers her own archive of Meridian — every recording she ever smuggled, including her only memories of her mother. Wren and the waking archivists protest; she proceeds anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship — she gives away the story of herself.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Alternating Oscar and Dax POVs, converging. As the gate opens, Dax arrives not to arrest her but to fly point through customs interdiction, going rogue at last. Gravity lurches a second time — the nine seconds repeating as the gate tears loose — and the colony ship threads the closing window. Emotional beat: climax; chaos, trust, and the exhilaration of a chosen family in freefall.

chapters.title: The Last Echo, Anew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. On the far side, Oscar remembers nothing of Meridian — but the archivists wake her each morning with a recorded memory of her own life, given back one day at a time. Wren names the new settlement's archive after her. Emotional beat: resolution — memory lost, belonging kept; the echo continues in other voices.
